You may struggle a bit if you're someone who needs a hardcore format of what to do because he's pretty wishy-washy about instructions. Just make sure to ask him to clarify what exactly is the A+ rubric and you'll be totally fine. Amazing teacher overall and his classes are super exciting to attend!

If you take ENGL101, make sure it's with Professor Daley. He makes the class super engaging, and most Fridays, there is no in-person class, and instead, there are asynchronous assignments, which you can finish pretty quickly. He is a very fair grader, and there is little to no busy work. There is an 8-10 page paper you need to write at the end, but it's not even that bad. Definitely recommend!

One of the best teachers I have ever had. He is super kind and genuinely cares about his students and their understanding and success within the material and not simply just churning out a gradable product. He was super understanding and gave us time when we needed it and doesn't take off points for late turn ins if you talk to him about an extension. He has a lot of interesting thoughts and just wants people to talk in his class. We spent the entire semester working towards this one research essay and project and the majority of the classwork was answering discussion questions aimed at helping us develop and get deeper into our topic. I'd take his class again.

Super chill guy and grades pretty leniently as long as you meet the requirements. Also is super lenient about deadlines and is more than willing to give you an extension if you ask. Only downside is the amount of random assignments leading up to essays. Overall, pretty easy class and as long as you put in a little effort on writing assignments you should be fine.

Arielle is an amazing instructor for this course, she always knows how to answer your questions, she is very understanding and relatable, and overall she just made this course better as a whole. You can tell that she cares about her job, and genuinely wants to help her students, she is easy going with grading, but can see through any BS, which is what I personally think makes a good teacher. She is incredibly smart and helped me immensely during this course, this is one of those classes I was really sad about leaving, simply because she is so great.

I would recommend her again and again, unfortunately I have no reason to take more English classes, but if I did, I would try to get in her class again. If you have a chance to take her class please do.

She's really nice, and I liked her a lot as a professor, but the way assignments are organized is bad. She will often tell you something in class that conflicts with the assignment she posted on Canvas, like not having to go into a certain aspect of it that you wouldn't have known. There are also 2 big essay assignments, which take 2-3 weeks to do, and she grades harsher than you would think.

A big plus for me is that near the end of the semester, she would do more and more Zoom classes, which is great since her classes are normally just her reading slides anyway.

Im gonna be honest and say that shes more of a 4.5. Shes a very good professor, extremely chill, lenient, and overall grades very fairly. Comparatively speaking, she gets a 4.5 bc some of the stuff i've heard from other people is that their engl101 professors are horrid, so shes 1000% the best option. HOWEVER, some things to note

She does not review our writing, someone else named nicole cochran does. She also is a slow grader, maybe the slowest I've ever had. Other then this tho, shes the best option for ENGL101. For this gened, i recommend her 1000%

Professor Cote is one of the best ENGL101 instructors you can take. He has a labor-based grading system that guarantees you an A as long as you turn in your work and show effort. He is VERY lenient with turning in assignments late and requesting extensions. He does not penalize you for trying new writing techniques or styles and encourages it. As long as you do the bare minimum, you will do just fine in the class. Highly recommend Professor Cote as he is a very kind and understanding person!!

Amazing professor. In Taina's class, I always felt welcome. It was very easy to talk to her whenever you had an issue with a grade or some sort of assignment, she created an environment where English101 was actually fun, and honestly I never liked english, but I would retake this class if it was with her. She was a very fair grader, she offers good constructive criticism while not actually killing your grade for one mistake. She is very sweet and clearly cares about her students. If you are taking English101, take it with her, you will not regret it

Professor Orefice is literally the GOAT. She was so sweet to all of her students and so chill. Prof O was really lenient on deadlines and late work, which was such a blessing. She gave us a lot of time in class to work on our big assignments like the position paper and inquiry essay. She's also a really fair grader so as long as you try, you'll do perfectly fine.

She also always brought snacks and treats, which was so kind of her! Prof O responded to emails really quickly as well. She's such a great professor, definitely take her class :)

Professor Hatcher is not a bad professor; I'm very confused why everyone is saying he grades harshly. He didn't grade harshly at all -- literally everything is graded for participation except for the position paper (which he also grades pretty lightly). I'm also confused about why people are complaining that he breaks everything down like we're in elementary school; that was a plus for me. It made everything much simpler, and I was able to focus on other harder classes. He can be a little sarcastic at times, but it's all fun and games, nothing serious. The one thing I would recommend is to go to class, as the scholars section is tiny (about 9 people in a class), so he cares about attendance a lot. He also allows extra time for essays. If you just take a picture with someone in the class, you can tell they want everyone in the class to be friends. Other professors in English grade off of quality and require you to actually do the remediation project, while he just requires you to do a reflection of it, not to do the actual project. Overall, this class was not bad at all, and everything is literally graded on participation; you don't have to be an amazing writer to get an A in this class.

Great professor. She does a really great job at preparing us for papers and projects. For major papers, she gives you a 24 hour grace period before points are taken off which is really nice. She also tries to adjust how some assignments work based on suggestions from her students that sometimes result to some confusion. However, she's pretty easy to reach out to and understanding of these issues.

Since English is a required class, I went into this course not expecting much, especially because it is usually not my favorite subject, but Professor Montroso completely changed that. His lectures are engaging and easy to listen to, and he explains ideas in a way that actually makes the material interesting. He also changes up how the required assignments are done, so you are not just writing papers the entire semester. We worked on things like a website, a video, and more traditional writing, which made the class feel much more creative and less repetitive. He is approachable, fair, and gives thoughtful feedback, and grading feels reasonable as long as you put in real effort. He creates a comfortable classroom environment where people actually want to participate, and even though English is required, this is genuinely a class worth taking.

Radford is an extremely nice guy who is always understanding, especially if needing an extension.  While he was very laidback in class, like others have mentioned, he can be a harsh grader and never gave out a perfect score on any paper or major assignment.  At least for my class, he graded things very late, usually weeks after it was due, but provided helpful feedback.  You don't really have to do the readings, but participation is graded, which includes raising your hand, commenting in zoom chat, and turning in assignments on time, even if points are directly taken off.  Overall, he is not the worst english professor you can take for ENGL101, and the half in person/half on zoom may be helpful to some.

Taina is a great and really chill professor. Unlike the one three-star, I found her class extremely easy if you had taken a high school English class. She was not 'too' harsh, but rather expected college students to write as college students. She wanted essays with subsidence and flow, which, for a college student, should not be too much. Taina clearly labeled her Canvas page and frequently updated students about upcoming deadlines. Although there were many 'busy work assignments,' this was due to the requirements mandated for ENGL101 at UMD. If you want an ENGL101 teacher who genuinely cares about you as a person, I 100% recommend Taina.

id love to put an expected grade but she dosent grade ANYTHING. the semester is over and i have NO IDEA what my grade is. she was super chill and class was easy but like you have no idea where your grade stands and also you're gonna learn nothing from this class. but she was chill
This guy fucking rocks. Just take him.

I had Dr. K for the fall 2025 semester. We had class triweekly with one day on zoom where he was usually available to confrence over zoom. Class was cancelled once a week on average. Dr. K is a super understanding and kind professor who will give you an extension as long as you communicate with him. He is a pretty easy grader as long as you put in the work. I recommend him!

Overall very friendly and kind teacher, I was between 4-5 stars. The class (ENGL101) is definitely a lot of work and assignments can be time consuming, but if you show up to lectures and put in some effort you'll be good. She cares about her students and actually wants to engage with you so if you give that back, she'll appreciate it. she learns everyone's name quick and marks if you are absent from class but idk if that actually effects your grade in any way. She also loves participation so if you raise your hand during class/ literally just show her you're listening, you'll have a good relationship. The in-person classes could be slow sometimes, but weren't too bad. There's a decent amount of group discussion/ peer review during class and she occasionally gives you time to work on assignments during the lecture which is nice. There are weekly freewrites (in class) & exit tickets for participation points... MAKE SURE TO DO THESE super easy points and not worth the dent in your grade if you don't. She does 1 on 1 conferences mid-semester to check-in and is good about responding to email. Her office hours are online 1 on 1 as well if you ever want to review work with her. 

Canvas was a little hard to follow at times as deadlines would occasionally change or assignments would be listed twice but she always clarified in class when something was different, just dont be afraid to ask if you're confused abt something, she's pretty understanding. I took this class first semester and thought it really helped improve my writing. Would recommend if you're willing to try and don't despise English - assignments are the same for ENGL101 regardless of who ur professor is.

While the rubrics and instructions for the assignments can be confusing, and she isn’t great at answering questions, the class isn’t bad. Professor Adeyemi is a very nice person, super impressive, and has a lot of knowledge to share, and personally I thought her grading was fair.

Prof. G is great, but also super weird so like be prepared for that. The class is super focused on Beowulf and Tolkien which made me nervous, because I didn't like either, but the class ended up being super chill. This is probably the English 101 class with the least writing done in the whole UMD. We only wrote one essay as the final paper. He often cancelled class once a week and almost always ends early. My friends had to write tons of long essays and had 5x the amount of work I had. Be prepared for some weird bits, curse words, fake Jeff Bezos calls in class, fairy stories, Beowulf and almost no work. Overall I recommend this class, but know he is not a generous grader and because of the lack of assignments I barely managed an A and most people probably got A-,B+,B. He often gives out 90s for big assignments and 49/50 for completion assignment without really explaining why/ providing a rubric in advance. He is a nice guy (kinda weird) and if you can do office hours before or after class he is happy to help, but didn't really make time otherwise. 

If you are gonna be busy with a lot of work from other classes, lazy or don't want to write and are okay with an A- and laughing at some bad jokes take the class!
english 101 is a waste of time, but this professor made it worth my while. they encouraged us to think out of the box and push ourselves intellectually, and took the time to get to know us.

Dr. K is a great professor. He's very nice and approachable and always happy to help if you ask him in person or on zoom on online days. There are 5 major writing assignments and a bunch of tiny assignments that are usually fast and easy to complete. I'd say he's a pretty lenient grader. It does take him a long time to get grades back but if you put some work in, you usually don't have to worry about your grades anyway.

Absolutely take Professor Montroso! He is the best professor I had this semester by far! He loves teaching and he's super helpful with every assignment. He's super understanding with late work and any issues you might have. I don't even like English and I genuinely looked forward to going to his class every day. You are missing out if you don't take his class!
Dr. Cote really is one of the kindest and most patient teachers I've ever had. He really cares about students and was fantastic with responding to questions that I emailed.
very nice teacher, but she asks a lot of questions during lectures and it can get kinda awkward. also, she takes a while to grade stuff.

She's one of the few professors who are passionate about what they teach and actually want you to learn instead of just getting done with a gen ed. Her lectures may seem "boring" but she's really just teaching the ENGL101 syllabus, which indeed is somewhat boring. She is one of the most helpful professors one can get (I have like 20 emails of her giving feedback to me whenever I asked her and she would reply very quickly). Her grading is not harsh at all. The comments you see saying her class is boring, might just be frustated of the attendence policy. Which is completely understandable, but you are here to attend classes are you not?

Very chill professor who really just wants to help you improve your writing. Always looking to help and always wants people to participate in class. Can be a tough grader, and there is sometimes a decent amount of work, but he is very understanding of your workload and will help you if needed. Overall, really great professor.

assigns assignments up until finals week bruh like this is english 101 I promise we don't need to be doing all this. wrote like 8 papers throughout the semester. shes pretty nice though, and its not hard to get a good grade, amount of work just gets annoying

Professor Roe isn't your typical college professor; rather, she gives more high school teacher vibes than a professor, and I mean that in the best way possible. In college, most professors don't care about you. They know you are an adult now, and they expect you to be fully taking care of yourself. In a sea of this, Professor Roe was a breath of fresh air. She knew all of us by our names, checked up on us to see how we were doing, and was really understanding if a student was going through tough times. She would always take input from students and use it to improve. However, something she always did do was call out students in the middle of the class (sometimes not always) and ask them questions, so pay attention in class, or just have an idea of what's going on, and you'll be good. In addition, she was very liberal with extensions. There were many times during the semester when I was not doing well, and she immediately granted extensions without asking any further questions. She also gave every student a free 24-hour extension on all major submissions. This 24-hour extension came in clutch during midterms week. In addition, she was very, very organized. She had a Google doc, which literally had what was due for that day, what we would be doing that day in class, and also what HW she would be assigning that day. She updated that sheet every day. So whenever I missed a class, I would just check the Google doc to see what happened. Oh yeah, and the best part was our class was MWF but she just made the Wednesday class asynchronous for the entire semester! So effectively, we all just met on two days only! 

Maybe something I didn't like that much was that she would often make us work in groups and interact with others a lot in class. I am an introvert, so I usually wasn't a big fan of this. I heard almost all other English professors do this, so maybe it's fine, but I sometimes felt like she loved making students work together or talk in class. Some may love this I personally wasn't the biggest fan of it. But again, all other professors also do it. 

Coming to the class, it did actually require a bit of work. Here is how the portion breakdown went: 
Participation: 15%
Major Assignment #1: Summary + Draft Workshop: 10%
Major Assignment #2: Rhetorical Analysis + Draft Workshop: 10%
Research Mini-Projects: 10%
Major Assignment #3: Inquiry Essay + Draft Workshop: 15%
Major Assignment #4: Position Paper + Draft Workshop: 25%
Major Assignment #5: Public Remediation Project + Draft Workshop: 15%

Participation is key here. It's not about how active you are in class, but literally if you submit notes on readings and provide peer reviews. If you do the bare minimum, she gives you 10/10 for every participation. I did miss a few participations where she immediately gave me a zero. I then submitted a project a bit late and told her in class that I did submit it late, and she immediately changed the grade to 10/10. So here's my suggestion: if you see anything marked as a participation submission, please just do it, it's literally free marks. Another big suggestion I have is, don't just submit your assignment directly when you are done. Rather, once you are done with a major assignment, send it to either the TA, Professor Roe, or the writing department and ask for feedback. After I started doing this, I got some feedback and started incorporating it in my work, and my grade began to increase, so yeah, that was a good idea. 

The goal of the class is to write a position paper with over 20 cited sources. Rather than making us find all 20 resources at once, Professor Roe slowly made us find 5 resources every few weeks, helping us slowly build towards it while also ensuring we never felt too overwhelmed trying to find any sources, so that was also nice. She also tried ensuring we never felt too overwhelmed with the work and if we did, we could just tell her and she would look to reduce it! 

Also, something important was that she trusted all of us. Many and I mean many, English professors started going crazy after AI came into play. Some of my friends were forced to write their position by hand in class, while some were forced to turn in their papers through rigorous AI checkers. Professor Roe trusted her students, and we weren't forced to turn in our papers through some weird tools.

Overall, great professor, go for her if you can.

CB was so sweet, organized, flexible with extensions, and she always answered emails in a timely manner. She's a great professor overall and it's clear that she really knows what she's talking about. The only downside is that she does grade kinda harshly (especially when you compare her grade distribution to other engl101 profs). Like another review said, it's difficult to get above like a 93% on major writing assignments, which does make getting an A/A+ difficult. You need to really make sure to turn in the smaller assignments on time and to do them decently, and to also do well on the major assignments to have a shot at an A. I took AP lit and lang in high school and found them to be easy, but definitely found it more difficult to get an A in this class. She is super approachable, though, so you can always go to her with issues or concerns about your writing. overall, if you're the kind of person that stays on top of your work and is a decent writer, CB is so caring and is the prof for you!

Ms Brie is a grad student who genuinely care about you as a person. She is accommodating and is not a harsh grader at all. This class was not something to stress about at all, and do not be surprised if class gets out early or is canceled somewhat frequently
best teacher I had this semester

Arielle is a great teacher, she is kind and patient. Outstanding professor, cannot recommend him enough for any course. Kind, caring, honest, generous and funny. He made class very enjoyable, was available for help at all times, granted extensions when necessary and went out of his way to support people who did not participate as much. Lenient grader who believes in providing only necessary feedback. His jokes were top-tier throughout the semester and his energy was infectious. He also brought us food thrice!! Overall, Professor Bhardwaj is legendary. Take a class with him.

It was her first semester teaching native English speakers, so she was probably more lenient with grading. She is clearly very passionate about teaching and writing, but going to lecture is completely unnecessary. Show up for the first day and then just do the assignments, and you get an A.

Very interesting guy. Very vocal and illuminated. He makes the class very interactive and engaging and there is barley any assignments. From that aspect it is an easy class. However, when trying to just complete an assignment sometimes he made it overly complicated and dragged it out.

Pretty chill class overall, but it is somewhat repetitive if you've already taken AP or IB Lang/Lit. Super easy professor. He made the course super easy to follow along and graded assignments very easily. If you submit a paper or task on time with decent effort, you’ll get an A. I would recommend him for ENGL101  as he’s very easy and accommodating.

William Pittman is a wonderful professor to have for ENGL101 as he makes the class feel like more than just an English gen-ed that you take and pass, I would recommend him wholeheartedly. 

You might go into this class thinking that as an English gen-ed it's a bunch of reading boring novels, writing busywork, and annotating papers just to trash them once you leave class. While some of that is present due to still being ENGL101 after all, professor Pittman meaningfully designs assignments in a way that they actually build off one another and make you better at writing as a result. 

In the beginning of class, he makes everyone get up and have a short socialization activity that is somewhat forced, but does help you get to know your classmates better (which given this is probably your first semester, is actually very beneficial). He will then usually lecture about some reading or his method of writing that he wants you to follow, which is actually very interesting. The two main things he teaches is 1-3-1 essay structure and the "microcosmic example" which he completely made up himself (you may see it elsewhere on the internet, and I can ensure you it's under one of his pen names) and helps your essay. 

His grading of essays is very lenient compared to past teachers I have had, where if you follow the format he wants 1:1 and have some semblance of a point, you'll probably get an A or B. This is great as a STEM major, because the rigid format makes your essays very formulaic to write and not require flowery language/structure (if you like this you may have a harder time). Your main assignment throughout the semester is writing this 20-paragraph essay that is about some Constitutional conflict in the US today, which may sound difficult but I assure you he will assist you however much you need. Basically you examine both sides (likely the left/right of the political spectrum) and argue for both completely impartially. At the end of the semester you get to make a 5 paragraph addendum where you get to argue your side, which is vindicating. 

While the class is great and Will Pittman is a lovable and somewhat quirky character who wants the best for his students, he does have some quirks that drop him short of 5 stars. He only grades assignments with a letter grade instead of a percentage, which is somewhat fine in of itself but on top of this he also just doesn't add any grades to ELMS, not even a single one. This leads to you not knowing your grade in the class at any point aside from general vibe based on previous assignments you've gotten back. This is extremely frustrating, and only fine because Pittman grades very leniently if you do things his way, so when you have an A in the class you'll probably know it.

In general, this class is a great contrast from the expectation for ENGL101 and William Pittman is a great professor who is every bit invested in your success in his class.
